pages.title: Al-Arafah Islamic International School & College (A Home of Moral & Modern Education)

sections.heading: Purpose and Objectives
paragraphs: Allah Subhanahu Ta'ala created human beings as 'Ashraful Makhluqat' (Best of the creation) and He made Islam His Approved Deen as the complete code of conduct for the entire mankind. Allah Rabbul A'lamin sent Prophets to convey His message. Prophet Mohammad (Sallallahu Alaihi wa sallam) is the last Prophet; there is no Prophet after him.

Those who will obey the commandments of Allah Ta'ala as revealed through His Prophets and lead their lives according to the Holy Quran and the Sunnah will be successful in this life and the eternal life after death. Allah Rabbul A'lamin has made acquiring of knowledge of His Deen compulsory for all men and women.

Al-Arafah Islamic Int'l School & College was established in 1998 under the welfare Project of Al-Arafah Islami Bank Foundation to foster the greater cause of Islamic education with an eye on the internationally recognized modern education. The degradation of moral and ethical values in our society and the current materialistic approaches to education pose a big threat to the new generation. The effort of this institute is to guide our youngsters towards the blissful Path of Almighty Allah and at the same time to provide them with the necessary knowledge and skills needed for leading a moral and honorable life.

sections.heading: Akhirat-oriented Faith-based Education
paragraphs: Allah Ta'ala advises us to seek His blessings for this world and the world hereafter. Unfortunately, we become too much involved in the worldly interests; some of us either totally forget Akhirat, or remain indifferent to the teachings of Islam. Our effort is, therefore, to introduce and nurture Akhirat-oriented faith-based education.

sections.heading: Education based on Imaan
paragraphs: How to protect ourselves from the Western malady and consequences thereof? One way may be to evolve an educational system, curriculum and syllabus to make our kids Faithful, Muttaqi and Akhirat-oriented and at the same time to provide them with modern faith-based education that will turn them into resourceful professionals in the mainstream of socio-economic life and worldly gains too.

sections.heading: Islamic Mind and Man
paragraphs: Under the present context, it would be expedient to maintain the syllabus followed by internationally recognized English medium schools and at the same time to add our own ideological subjects which will turn our children into faithful (Imander) Muslims in their attitudes, thoughts, mentality and conscience. The children will then be pious Muslims in faith and conviction, and also followers of Sunnah in culture. Hopefully, their destination will be Jannah, Insha-Allah.

sections.heading: Hifzul Quran Section
paragraphs: We have already introduced our Hifzul Quran Section (Al-Arafah Tahfizul Quran Madrasah) entirely dedicated to make a child a perfect Hafiz of the Holy Quran. During its first stage, (Junior Section) a student studies general subjects like English Language, Literature, Math, Science, Bangla, Arabic, etc. But at the time of memorization, a student will study only English, Maths & Bangla so that they can get maximum time to memorize the Holy Quran with greater concentration. Students can get themselves admitted in the Junior Section at the age of 4-6 & its duration will be 3/4 years (Nur. - Std. I). In case of fulltime Hifz, they can start at the age of 7-10.

sections.heading: Computer Education
paragraphs: Today, Information Technology (IT) is the fastest growing industry in the world. With this view in mind, we are committed to equip our students with useful knowledge and skills of computer. So, computer has been introduced as a compulsory subject in AIISC right from Standard II.
sections.note: This paragraph continues across pages 02 and 03.

sections.heading: Salient Features
bullets: While imparting knowledge to students, we pay particular attention to the development of individual talent.
We train our students in computer and make them aware of the latest technological advancements.

We try to provide an Islamic environment wherein the moral and spiritual self of the student develops under the teachings of the Holy Quran and Sunnah and thus make them responsible to family, society, state and above all, to the Almighty Allah.
We encourage co-curricular activities including games, sports and cultural program.

sections.heading: Admission Procedure
paragraphs: Normally, admission is open from December to January. However, depending on the availability of seats and the suitability of students admission is offered throughout the year. Students need to face an admission test at the pre-determined dates and time. There may also be special cases under special circumstances for admission. The authority reserves the right of admission.
items: a) Any student, seeking admission to Al-Arafah Islamic Int'l School & College, is to collect an admission form and the prospectus from the admission office on payment of Tk. 300/= (non refundable).
b) The filled-in Form, along with 3 passport size photographs of the applicant, will have to be submitted to the office and thereafter, Admit Card for admission test will be given.
c) Candidates, successful in written, viva and aptitude test will have to qualify in medical check-up.

d) Student found fit for admission will have to submit his birth certificate, transcript of previous school (if applicable), parents photographs one each, and pay admission and other fees at a time or in pre-determined installments (if any). On completion of the above procedure, a student can be admitted to the desired class with the approval of the appropriate authority.
e) Admission of any student can be cancelled without assigning any reason.
sections.note: Item d) continues from page 03 onto page 04.

sections.heading: Renewal of Admission
paragraphs: Every student will have to renew admission every year on payment of re-admission fee and on fulfillment of other conditions as stated below:
items: a) the student seeking re-admission will have on record at least 75% attendance in the previous class/year.
b) the result of the previous class test is satisfactory.
c) the overall conduct of student is satisfactory.
sections.closing: Principal will have the authority to reject any re-admission without assigning any reason.

subsections.heading: Play Group
paragraphs: There is no formal admission test for Play group. However, the principal will have an oral interview with the parents and the child before the admission is offered. Since seats are limited, admission is offered on first come, first serve basis. If seats are filled up, there shall not be further admission unless the number of additional students seeking admission constitutes a group of ten for whom additional teacher might be arranged. Admission to the following classes will be ensured through an assessment test on the subjects mentioned:

subsections.heading: Nursery
items: a) English Alphabet (Capital and Small).
b) Number (1 to 50).
c) Bangla Alphabets (Vowels Only).

sections.heading: Syllabus for Admission Test (continued)

b) Mathematics.

sections.note: Note: For admission tests in KG to Std-X, syllabus of the previous class will be followed.

subsections.heading: Educational Facilities
paragraphs: Al-Arafah Islamic Int'l School & College is a unique institution providing Islamic and modern education in English medium in an Islamic environment. Here students from Play Group to O' level are taught in English medium along with Bangla and Arabic of appropriate level.

subsections.heading: Library
paragraphs: The institution provides a well equipped library for teachers and students. Academic texts, reference books and books for pleasure are available here. Students can borrow certain books from the library. Besides, Al-Arafah Islamic Bank Foundation is maintaining a big resourceful library of Islamic books at 32 Topkhana Road, Dhaka, which the teachers and the senior students of AIISC can access to.

sections.heading: Lab Facilities
paragraphs: We have a Science Lab and a separate Computer Lab to enhance practical knowledge of our students in the respective fields of their studies.

sections.heading: Digi Class Facilities
paragraphs: Al-Arafah Islamic International School & College has recently introduced digitally classroom facilities. DigiClass is a wonderful award-winning multimedia-enabled teaching tool that makes the lessons effective and enjoyable. It also empowers teachers to customize teaching sessions and lessons and keep the learners' pace in mind for a more comprehensive understanding of the texts.

The multimedia contents of the DigiClass include all the syllabus of Edexcel from KG - II to A' Level. Students can enjoy their lessons through the 3D interactivity of demonstrations, rhymes, games, e-books, etc of various texts.

sections.heading: Residential Facility
paragraphs: Currently hostel facilities are available for the fulltime Hifz students only (deserving ones). Students stay here in homely atmosphere under the supervision of our experienced and caring teachers. We have set weekly standard food menu for a balanced and nutritious diet. There are also indoor games facilities for the fulltime Hifz students.

sections.heading: Transport Facility
paragraphs: Our school buses ply on predetermined routes. If adequate number of students is available, transport may be arranged on new routes. Every bus is carefully conducted by an experienced practicing Muslim driver with a caring lady attendant to ensure the safety of the kids.

sections.heading: Academic Calendar
paragraphs: Academic Year is from January to December. Programs of regular classes, co-curricular activities, and exam schedules as well as holidays and events on the days of historical, national and religious significance are orderly set in the year planner. Accordingly, students are given Academic Calendars at the beginning of the year.

sections.heading: Parents-Teachers Meeting
paragraphs: Regular meetings of the parents and teachers are arranged to discuss and evaluate the activities of the students. We feel that parents are an important part of the institution, and their constructive suggestions are, therefore, gladly received. Parents/guardians with prior appointment may also speak to the teachers personally, if necessary.

sections.heading: Parents-Teachers meetings meet the following objectives
bullets: Exchange of views between parents and teachers about the students.
Contribution of teachers and parents to the children's improvement in morality.
Sharing success of the students and the institution.
Providing a forum for new ideas; and
Improvement in the quality of education.

sections.heading: The Curriculum
paragraphs: Al-Arafah Islamic Int'l School & College offers education from Play Group to O' Level in both streams - science and commerce. The School is on its gradual lead to A' Level. Its aim is to combine Islamic values and contemporary knowledge.

sections.intro: Activities planned around the academic curriculum to make the overall development of the kids include personal, social and emotional development, language, literacy and communication, mathematics, knowledge and understanding of the world, physical development and creative development. We aim to support all children and strive to develop their potential at their own pace.

sections.heading: Communication, Language and Literacy
items: 1. Encourage children, both in small and large groups, to extend their vocabulary and fluency by talking and listening, and by hearing and responding to stories, songs, rhymes and text books.

2. Provide a well-stocked book corner to give every child the opportunity and inspiration to become familiar with books and enjoy them, be able to handle them and be aware of their uses both for reference and pleasure.

sections.heading: Personal, Social, and Emotional Development
items: 1. Support children individually, in a nurturing environment, to develop confidence, autonomy and self-respect.
2. Encourage children to work and concentrate independently and also to take part in groups, sharing and cooperating with other children and adults.
3. Provide activities, conversation and practical examples so that they can learn acceptable ways to express their feelings and have respect for the feelings of others.
4. Teach children the sense of responsibility for themselves, their property, and for the social groups as members of the community.

sections.heading: Mathematical Development
items: 1. Provide adult-supported practical experiences to enable children to become familiar with sorting, matching, ordering, sequencing and counting activities, which form the basis for early mathematics.
2. Assist children to learn and use the vocabulary of mathematics, identifying objects by shape, position, size, volume and number.
3. Teach the use of simple mathematical operations.

sections.heading: Knowledge and Understanding of the World
items: 1. Provide a wide range of natural and manufactured study materials to help children explore and experiment knowledge in a safe and stimulating environment.
2. Help children to observe the features of objects and substances, recognizing differences, patterns and similarities, and share their findings.
3. Assist children in exploring and understanding their environment, both within the group and in the wider community.
4. Provide a range of safe and well-maintained equipment to enable children to extend their technical understanding.
5. Use simple tools and techniques as appropriate to achieve their intentions and solve problems.

sections.heading: Physical Development
items: 1. Provide a range of indoor and outdoor equipment and opportunities to help children develop confidence and enjoyment in the use and development of their body skills.
2. Maintain a high level of adult supervision to enable children to meet physical challenges safely and develop skills.
3. Support children in the development of fine motor skills required to use tools, including pens and pencils, and to handle small objects with increasing control and precision.

sections.heading: Creative Development
items: 1. Encourage children to use a wide range of resources in order to express their own ideas and feelings and construct their individual responses to real life experience.

2. Use art equipment, including paint, glue, crayons and pencils, as well as natural and discarded resources, to give open ended exploration of color, shape and texture and develop skills of painting, drawing and collage.
3. Give children the opportunity to become involved in and respond to rhymes and stories.
4. Provide opportunities for imaginative role-play, both individually and in a group.
sections.note: Items 2 to 4 appear at the top of page 10.

sections.heading: Assembly & PT
paragraphs: Assembly and PT are regularly arranged to teach students discipline and punctuality to ensure their physical and mental development. Moreover, recitation from the Holy Quran, National Anthem, Oath taking and Islamic manners are also practiced in the assembly to make children patriotic Muslims.

sections.heading: Tiffin & Salah Break
paragraphs: A short break is given for tiffin and offering Zuhur Salah in the school premises. Boys and girls perform their Salah separately under the supervision of their respective male and female teachers. Thus they are guided to become practicing Muslims in the real life.

sections.heading: Co-curricular Activities
paragraphs: We organize different competitions such as debate, Qirat competition, Quiz (knowledge of current affairs and Islamiat), extempore speech, set speech, annual sports and cultural events on specified occasions. Study tours, excursions and picnics are also arranged annually.

sections.heading: Islamic Orientation Program
paragraphs: Psychologists say that the causes of degradation of the Western society are the lack of moral teachings, detachment from the family and the effects of erotic and violent films. We believe that there is only one remedy for these ills of societies and the children must develop this remedy according to Islamic morality. We arrange Islamic orientation programs for the students to teach them the basics of Islam, aiming at making them responsible to the Almighty Allah, the nation and the fellow citizens. Besides, we ensure a full Islamic environment in the institution.
sections.note: This paragraph continues across pages 10 and 11.

sections.heading: English Language Club
paragraphs: To develop English language skills there is an English Language Club in the School. Since 2006, the Language Club is running with the enthusiastic participation of a group of students and teachers. The club publishes a language magazine annually. Students are contributing articles to run the English language magazine. The magazine contains varieties of interesting topics, including Letters to Editor. It helps the children enjoy the right of democracy - the freedom of speech. Writing stories, poetry, jokes, and of the individual experiences, general knowledge, etc. all help to develop the writing skills of the students. English language club consists of 30 members of different classes. The main aim of the language club is to maintain English language environment in School area.
sections.note: This paragraph continues across pages 11 and 12.

sections.heading: Enrolment with British Council
paragraphs: The institution enrolled itself to the 'Young Learners Centre' in British Council Library. British Council holds different competition programs among the English medium schools. Our students already have participated in two such programs: Art competition on 'Environmental Pollution' arranged by Commonwealth countries through British Council. Three of our students participated and one of them, Sultana Akter of Std-III won the 1st position in the competition. On weekly holidays our students go to 'Young Learners Centre' to read books, use Internet and take DVDs on educational films.

sections.heading: Teacher Training by British Council
paragraphs: We always keep our teachers updated with the most effective teaching techniques and methodologies through in house and outside teacher training programs as well as workshops. Besides, our teachers attend training courses regularly on the subjects of their specialization and teaching methodologies conducted by the British Council of Bangladesh. In fine, we are always committed to provide our kids with the best of education through our experienced teachers.
